item.description: The origin and early radiation of winged insects (Pterygota) represent one of the most transformative events in terrestrial evolution, yet phylogenetic relationships among their basalmost lineages (Ephemeroptera, Odonata and Neoptera) continue to be a central debate within insect systematics. Here, we present the most taxonomically comprehensive phylogenomic analysis to date, leveraging genomic and transcriptomic data from 101 species, including 16 sequenced ephemeropteran genomes. Employing 1,367 universal single-copy orthologs across two supermatrices, we used concatenation- and coalescent-based frameworks under homogeneous and heterogeneous, and multispecies coalescent models. Our analyses support Palaeoptera monophyly. Although coalescent-based methods initially suggested a Chiastomyaria (Ephemeroptera + Neoptera) topology, subsequent signal dissection and topology tests confirm that the preponderance of genomic signal favors a monophyletic Palaeoptera. Furthermore, we identify incomplete lineage sorting and gene tree estimation error as the primary drivers of previous topological conflicts. Our molecular dating results point to an Early Devonian origin of crown-Pterygota, whereas crown-Palaeoptera first emerged in the Late Devonian. By reconciling molecular evidence with morphological synapomorphies, such as wing-base sclerite homologies, this study provides a coherent framework for the early evolution of winged insects, supports a single origin of wings, and identifies the neopteran wing-folding mechanism as a singular evolutionary innovation. item.title: Tracing missing copper: ultrapotassic rocks record isotopic evidence of crustal Cu depletion
item.dc:creator: Chen-Hao Luo
Wenli Liang
Rui Wang
Oliver Nebel

item.description: Post-subduction reactivation of metasomatized lithospheric mantle generates high-K shoshonitic magmas in the continental crust and has been suggested to be potentially associated with porphyry Cu mineralization, yet its role in the continental crustal Cu budget remains ambiguous. Here, we use Cu isotope analyses and geochemical modeling of Cenozoic ultrapotassic rocks from southern Tibet to show that variations in Th/La record a transition from mantle partial melting to magmatic differentiation, during which Cu behavior was controlled by sulfide retention in the source and fluid activity, respectively. During partial lithospheric mantle melting, residual solid sulfide phases retain Cu in the mantle source, generating Cu-depleted melts with slightly heavier δ⁶⁵Cu and potentially contributing to the Cu depletion of continental crust. Subsequently, exsolved fluids preferentially scavenge isotopically heavy Cu, causing both Cu contents and δ⁶⁵Cu values to decrease in the residual magmas. The Cu isotopic evolution of these ultrapotassic magmas differs from that of ore-bearing porphyries in the belt, potentially reflecting differences in magma source or evolutionary history. This study shows that residual sulfides in the lithospheric mantle can retain copper during ultrapotassic magmatism, limiting its transfer to the crust, while fluid activity controls Cu redistribution in evolved magmas. item.title: Physics-informed deep learning links geodetic data and fault friction
item.dc:creator: Rikuto Fukushima
Masayuki Kano
Kazuro Hirahara
Makiko Ohtani
item.description: Fault slip modeling, based on laboratory-derived friction laws, has significantly enhanced our understanding of fault mechanics. Agreement between model predictions and observations supports the hypothesis that observed slip diversity, including fast earthquakes and slow transient slips (Slow Slip Events; SSEs), originates from frictional heterogeneity. However, quantitative assessments of frictional heterogeneity from geodetic observations while fully incorporating fault mechanics are lacking due to the difficulties of high-dimensional optimization. In this study, we aim to address this gap using Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to link frictional heterogeneity with geodetic observations. PINNs employ a neural network to represent the spatially variable frictional properties, making their estimation feasible. Targeting the 2010 Bungo SSE in southwest Japan, our estimation reveals heterogeneous friction coinciding with localized SSE nucleation in southwest Shikoku, and subsequent westward propagation. The calculated fault slip of SSE successfully reproduces the spatio-temporal pattern of observed surface displacements. This PINN-based inversion provides a mechanically consistent fault slip model validated through quantitative comparison with observations. Furthermore, we forecast the future fault slip evolution, demonstrating the importance of assimilating observations spanning multiple SSE cycles. Our results demonstrate the potential of PINN for advancing understanding of fault mechanics and enabling physics-based fault slip forecasting. Spatially variable frictional properties along a fault can be estimated using a physics-informed neural network approach that enables physics-consistent slip modelling, as tested on the 2010 Bungo slow slip event in southwest Japan. item.description: Abstract Marine coastal systems are important for global biogeochemical cycling and are particularly sensitive to climate change effects due to their shallow depths, which results in rapid heat transfer to the sediments. Here we used one-year reciprocal in situ translocations of sediments between a Baltic Sea long-term (>50 years) warming-influenced bay and a nearby unaffected control bay to predict how the sediments and their associated bacterial communities may respond to future climate change and whether those changes were reversible. Geochemical parameters, methane plus sulfate profiles, and 16S rRNA gene-based bacterial diversity and community composition show partial convergence of the sediment-parameters to the translocated environment, suggesting climate change will rapidly alter bacteria communities of Baltic Sea coastal sediments. However, more pronounced responses in the control to the heated bay translocation direction suggest that while a return toward present-day conditions may be possible if climate change is reversed, such a recovery may be incomplete or require a longer time than one year. item.title: Onset of zircon decomposition during saprolitic weathering
item.dc:creator: Martin Yan Hei Li
Mei-Fu Zhou
item.description: Abstract Zircon is conventionally considered as refractory in supergene environments, enabling the preservation of geochemical records for tracing various Earth’s processes and the use of the zircon structure as a nuclear waste form. However, how refractory zircon is during weathering, especially when crystalline and in an early stage of weathering, is unknown. In this study, we demonstrate that crystalline zircon would start to weather during an early-stage saprolitic weathering. Nano-scale examination reveals that weathering of zircon proceeds through dissolution of primary, crystalline zircon and precipitation of secondary, amorphous zircon. Non-formula elements, like U, Th and heavy rare earth elements, are uptake and structurally incorporated in this process. Thereby, metamictisation of the zircon would accelerate and eventually promote the dissolution of zircon. In supergene environments, zircon would steadily weather, calling for further evaluation on the geological and environmental applications of zircon. item.title: Hydrogen isotopes reveal water leakage from the core
item.dc:creator: Yu Zhang
Wenzhong Wang
Zhongqing Wu
Bowen Chen
item.description: Chemical heterogeneities in Earth’s deep mantle may record either preserved primordial reservoirs or later core-mantle exchange, but distinguishing between these origins remains challenging. Hydrogen isotopes offer a sensitive tracer, yet whether magma ocean crystallization could generate a deuterium-depleted deep reservoir has not been quantitatively evaluated. Here, we use machine learning–accelerated path-integral simulations to determine equilibrium hydrogen isotope fractionation between silicate melt and bridgmanite, ringwoodite, and wadsleyite under magma ocean conditions. Incorporating these fractionation factors into a magma ocean crystallization model shows that mineral-melt fractionation is intrinsically weak, producing an essentially homogeneous D/H distribution in the primitive mantle. Magma ocean crystallization therefore cannot generate the extremely low δD values observed in some ocean island basalts. Combined with exceptionally high 3 He/ 4 He ratios, these signatures more plausibly reflect selective transfer of primordial volatiles from Earth’s core, implying sustained volatile exchange across the core-mantle boundary. item.title: The riverine land-to-ocean carbon flux
item.dc:creator: Robert G. M. Spencer
Travis W. Drake
Maodian Liu
Peter A. Raymond
item.description: The land-to-ocean export of carbon via rivers is a key component in the global carbon cycle. In this Review, we provide an overview of the factors governing the mobilization of carbon into rivers and those modulating riverine carbon export to the ocean. Terrestrial landscapes are estimated to deliver 3–4 PgC yr^−1 to inland waters, with the majority outgassed rather than exported to the ocean. Model estimates converge on a total global carbon export flux of 0.8–1.0 PgC yr^−1; however, regional, watershed and carbon species resolved estimates vary substantially owing to differences in source inputs, transport processes, biogeochemical transformations, and climate and hydrological drivers. Across the models that were synthesized, global estimates for individual carbon species span approximately a threefold difference, whereas estimated export of some species to the Atlantic and Pacific basins varies by up to fivefold. The Amazon and Congo together contribute approximately 21% of global river discharge, yet remain far less observed than many smaller temperate watersheds; the world’s 30 largest rivers by discharge account for approximately half of global cumulative river discharge. Therefore, expanding observations is clearly a priority to reduce uncertainties in modelled land-to-ocean carbon fluxes, and could be supported by the development of sensor networks and remote sensing observations to improve spatiotemporal resolution. Integrating these large datasets with mechanistic studies of biogeochemical modulators and machine learning approaches would inform understanding of carbon dynamics within major watersheds and improve predictions of this globally important carbon flux. Globally, rivers export ~10^15 grams of carbon to the ocean each year. This Review explores the mobilization, modulation and transport of different species of carbon within watersheds and rivers, with the aim to help inform and improve land-to-ocean carbon flux estimates. item.description: Nitrogen regulates primary productivity across much of the biosphere, yet fixed nitrogen loss remains poorly constrained because existing methods rely on indirect proxies or ex situ experiments. item.description: The mechanism driving accelerating unrest at the densely populated Campi Flegrei caldera since 2005 remains debated. Analyzing an unprecedented two-decade geochemical dataset, we show that escalating soil CO 2 fluxes closely tracks caldera uplift, revealing magmatic fluid pressurization at 3- to 4-kilometer depth and heating as the fundamental driver of the unrest. A critical magmatic gas pulse occurred between 2018 and 2022 specifically focused this outgassing beneath the Solfatara crater. Thermodynamic modeling demonstrates that an increasing mass of ascending fluid pressurizes the hydrothermal system, forcing vapor condensation within the upper kilometer. This condensation transfers latent heat to the crust. We calculate that this released thermal energy is an order of magnitude greater than that required for the 1.6-meter uplift since 2005. Ultimately, this fluid pressurization and heating drive accelerating deformation and seismicity; alongside the 2021 emergence of seismic sequences with short inter-event times, it directly signals an escalating phreatic or magmatic eruption risk. item.description: How mining has shaped long-term economic and political landscapes across Europe and the Mediterranean remains poorly understood, largely because archaeological evidence is spatially fragmented and ore sources are difficult to trace from atmospheric lead (Pb) records. Here, we compile Pb isotope data from environmental archives and introduce the Environmental Match Intensity Index (EMII), a metric applied to peat records to track Pb–silver (Ag) ore-supply patterns and relative changes in the integrated mining-related atmospheric Pb signal over six millennia. EMII reveals an early mining signal centered on Laurion (Greece) during the Late Neolithic/Chalcolithic, followed by Bronze Age expansion structured by maritime routes linking the Cyclades, the Troad, and Anatolian coasts. From the Iron Age onward, our results challenge the conventional Iberian-centered mining model and instead reveal a polycentric and multimodal organization rooted in west-central European districts interconnected through major fluvial corridors and complementary terrestrial and maritime routes. EMII reaches its first major peak during the Early Roman period, declines during Late Antiquity and the Early Middle Ages, and rises again from the High Middle Ages onward. Despite these temporal fluctuations, the overall continental distribution of the contributing mining regions remains broadly stable. By connecting environmental archives with mining, transport, and urban demand, this framework provides a scalable approach for reconstructing the long-term organization of metal production and circulation and their contribution to anthropization processes across different chrono-cultural periods and geographical settings. item.description: Mineral–organic interfaces regulate crystallization processes central to mineral evolution and biogeochemical cycling, yet how organic matter (OM) actively directs nucleation and growth pathways remains unresolved. item.description: Calcium carbonate (CaCO_3) plays a central role in the deep carbon cycle, yet its stability under varying oxygen fugacity ( f O_2) in the mantle wedge remains poorly constrained. item.description: Quartz-vein gold deposits dominate Earth’s gold endowment. However, the origin of their ore-forming fluids remains contested. While the traditional model invokes crustal metamorphism of silica-rich rocks, fluids derived from metasomatized mantle have emerged as a viable alternative. Yet how siliceous ore-forming fluids are released from this mantle source remains unclear. Here we propose that sub-solidus devolatilization of metasomatized mantle lithosphere generates siliceous hydrothermal fluids without partial melting, based on samples from the post-collisional Yangtze and North China craton margins. Silicon and oxygen isotope systematics show that both hypozonal (δ30Si = −0.30‰ to −0.20‰) and mesozonal gold deposits yield δ30Si values consistent with potassic mafic rocks, including lamprophyres, and metasomatized mantle sources. Integrated with a marked increase in mantle xenolith equilibration temperatures from pre- to post-mineralization in the Jiaodong gold province, phase-equilibrium calculations​ for the phlogopite-lherzolite system reveal a critical thermal window (700–800°C, 1–2 GPa) where​​ devolatilization and silicon release are maximized below the wet solidus. We demonstrate that silica-poor metasomatized mantle at 700–950°C releases fluids with Si solubility comparable to that of silica-rich lower crust at 400–700°C. This model incorporates solid-state fluid generation, a key feature of the crustal metamorphic model, and clarifies ​the origin and capacity of siliceous fluid production​ within the mantle-derived paradigm. It supports a scenario in which spatiotemporally associated quartz-vein gold ores and potassic mafic rocks are successive but independent products of mantle devolatilization and melting, respectively, as the thermal profile crosses the solidus. We conclude that this previously overlooked sub-solidus mantle devolatilization applies broadly to post-collisional and other orogenic gold systems. item.description: The giant Jiaojia gold deposit (>200 t Au) in the Jiaodong Peninsula, China, hosts three distinct mineralization styles: disseminated, breccia, and stockwork (orebodies I and II); thin pyrite-muscovite-quartz veins (orebody III); and auriferous quartz-sulfide veins (orebody IV). These styles are spatially controlled by a multiorder fault network. Integrated in situ textural, trace-element, and sulfur isotope analyses of pyrite reveal that these styles formed during a single hydrothermal event, with gold precipitation mechanisms varying systematically with structural setting. In the high-strain fault core and damage zone of the Jiaojia fault zone (orebodies I and II), extensive fluid-rock interaction and sulfidation dominated, producing pyrite enriched in Ag, As, Au, Bi, Cu, Pb, Sb, and Te, with heavier δ34S values (median 10.95‰) relative to those in orebodies III and IV. In contrast, steep faults within the secondary Baoli fault zone hosting orebody IV record lighter δ34S values (median 9.48‰) and porous pyrite with elevated Au/As ratios and broad trace-element variability, indicating rapid crystallization from fluids that underwent intense phase separation triggered by abrupt pressure drops. Orebody III, hosted in the transitional zone, displays mixed geochemical and isotopic characteristics, reflecting contributions from both sulfidation and phase separation. Overlapping homogenization temperatures of fluid inclusions from previous studies across orebodies rule out significant thermal gradients, demonstrating that fault zone architecture, by modulating sulfidation and fluid depressurization, was the primary control on gold precipitation. These findings establish a genetic model directly linking specific ore styles to their structural domains, providing a predictive framework for exploration. item.description: Abstract We integrate major and trace element data with high-precision Pb isotope analyses of ores from the Middle Miocene felsic volcanic-hosted massive sulfide deposits of northeast Japan, including the Matsumine-Shakanai, Furutobe, and Nurukawa deposits, to elucidate the distribution and source of precious metals. Matsumine-Shakanai shows highly variable and generally elevated Au (0.3–123 ppm) and Ag (6–5010 ppm), whereas Furutobe and Nurukawa display lower and more uniform values. Gold and Ag are hosted mainly by sulfosalts at Matsumine-Shakanai but occur predominantly as electrum at Furutobe and Nurukawa. The uranogenic 207 Pb/ 204 Pb vs. 206 Pb/ 204 Pb plot defines distinct clusters with a steep linear trend, indicating two metal source components: a relatively unradiogenic, juvenile source corresponding to the Middle Miocene volcanic rocks and a more radiogenic source attributed to pre-Miocene basement rocks. At Matsumine-Shakanai, correlations between 207 Pb/ 204 Pb and Zn, Pb, Au, and Ag suggest a dominant contribution from evolved basement rocks for these metals. Such relationships are absent at Furutobe and Nurukawa, suggesting that Au and Ag enrichments at these deposits were controlled by other processes, such as transport and depositional processes. Lead isotope maps reveal a north-south trend parallel to the Miocene fault systems, reflecting hydrothermal fluid pathways. Incorporating recent findings of petrological studies on the thermal evolution of volcanic host rocks, we propose a geological model that involves progressive heating of the shallow crust in an extensional setting, which resulted in rising of the isotherms and extraction of metals from an isotopically evolved source providing much of Zn, Au, and Ag and an isotopically juvenile source providing Cu. item.title: Genetic links between large-scale REE mineralization and intense differentiation of alkaline silicate magmas: Insights from the Weishan syenite‑carbonatite complex, China

item.description: Mantle-derived alkaline‑carbonatite complexes are the primary global source of rare earth elements (REE), yet the important factors promoting REE mineralization remain debated. In this study, we present an integrated investigation of the Weishan alkaline‑carbonatite complex in the North China Craton. The Weishan complex is dominated by Early Cretaceous (∼120 Ma) syenite, with subordinate carbonatite veins cutting both the syenite and surrounding country rocks. Economically significant REE mineralization is spatially associated with the carbonatite. The syenite and carbonatite share overlapping SrNd isotopic compositions [(87Sr/86Sr) i = 0.7065–0.7086, εNd(t) = −9.3 to −7.7], indicating derivation from a common enriched lithospheric mantle source. In addition, the syenitic rocks, including syenites and carbonated syenites, display pronounced light Mg isotopes, with δ26Mg values ranging from −1.60‰ to −0.21‰, implying that the mantle source had been metasomatized by recycled sedimentary carbonates. Protracted fractional crystallization of the magma produced highly evolved syenite and further amplified REE enrichment in the magmatic system. The syenites are characterized by high SiO2 and alkali contents, strong depletion in Mg, Fe, Ti, and Ca, high total REE concentrations (∼1614 ppm), and elevated (La/Yb)N ratios (50–565). Advanced differentiation is further recorded by Na-rich aegirine–augite rims in clinopyroxene and high REE contents in titanite from the syenite. Continued magmatic differentiation ultimately promoted the formation of REE-rich carbonate-bearing liquids, culminating in large-scale mineralization during the late magmatic to hydrothermal stages. These results demonstrate that carbonate-bearing alkaline magmas derived from an enriched mantle source and undergoing advanced differentiation are critical for REE fertility, with broader implications for the genesis of REE deposits in alkaline‑carbonatite provinces worldwide. item.dc:creator: Youqing Wei

item.description: The early India-Eurasia collision induced widespread tectonic deformation and vigorous magmatism throughout southern Tibet, yet the dynamic connections between magmatism and crustal evolution in the collision zone remain controversial. Here, we present new integrated datasets comprising zircon U-Pb geochronology, in situ zircon Hf-O isotopes, whole-rock major and trace element geochemistry, and bulk Sr-Nd isotopes for the Kazi volcanic sequence within the Paleocene–Eocene Pana Formation in the Namling area, southern Lhasa Terrane. Zircon U-Pb dating constrains synchronous eruption of bimodal basaltic-andesites and rhyolite lavas at ca. 48 Ma. Geochemical and isotopic results indicate that the basaltic-andesite magmas originated from subduction-metasomatized hybrid mantle sources, with insignificant crustal contamination and petrogenesis controlled by two-stage fractional crystallization. The contemporaneous rhyolites exhibit typical geochemical signatures of A-type granites, generated by low-pressure dehydration melting of juvenile felsic crustal materials. Consistently depleted Sr-Nd-Hf-O isotopic compositions reveal a predominant juvenile mantle contribution to the magmatic system. The newly identified ca. 48 Ma bimodal magmatism documents the complete breakoff of the Neo-Tethyan oceanic slab and marks a tectonic transition from compression to extension in southern Tibet. This magmatic event records a prominent Phanerozoic crustal growth episode on the Tibetan Plateau, providing robust constraints on the dynamic evolution of tectonic switching and crustal evolution in global collisional orogens. item.description: The Cunqian Cu-Pb-Zn deposit is a significant skarn-porphyry deposit located at the junction of the eastern and central segments of the Qin-Hang metallogenic belt (QHMB) in China. However, ore prospecting in this area has been hindered by insufficient research on ore-related intrusions relative to adjacent areas. To constrain the emplacement timing and magma sources of the ore-related intrusions, this study presents systematic zircon U-Pb ages, trace element compositions, and Lu-Hf isotopic data. Zircon U-Pb dating yields a Late Jurassic emplacement age (ca. 160 Ma) for the ore-related granodiorite porphyry. Hf isotopic compositions (εHf(t) = –9.8 to –6.7) and corresponding two-stage model ages (TDM2 = 1.6–1.9 Ga) of the same zircon population indicate derivation mainly from recycled Paleoproterozoic crustal components. Numerous inherited zircon cores (417–3102 Ma) are present, and the ca. 817 Ma group is particularly noteworthy for its elevated εHf(t) values (3.4–7.4), which indicate involvement of Neoproterozoic juvenile crustal components in the source region. Zircon trace elements indicate that the ore-related magmas exhibited moderately oxidized conditions (mean ΔFMQ = 0.94) and elevated magmatic water contents (7.92–11.0 wt.%), suggesting their formation from an oxidized and hydrous magma. Despite these oxidizing conditions being favorable for Cu-Au enrichment, the Pb-Zn-dominant metal assemblage of the deposit suggests that source composition, rather than redox conditions alone, exerted the primary control on the metal budget. Fertile magmatism derived from crustal sources may therefore favor Pb-Zn-rich mineralization even under oxidizing conditions, possibly reflecting magmatic evolution processes that limited Cu enrichment. The Cunqian deposit underscores the considerable Cu-Pb-Zn exploration potential of such transitional zones, where polymetallic mineralization associated with ancient crustal reworking is preferentially localized. item.description: Granite-related U deposits are generally spatially related to pre-existing granites with the crystallization ages of granites significantly earlier than the mineralization ages. The contribution of the pre-ore granitic magmatism to mineralization remains unclear. To address this issue, this study took the Lujing U deposit formed in Cretaceous–Paleogene as the research object. We carried out in situ geochronological and geochemical studies on apatite, monazite, and xenotime from the silicified fault zone, which was previously considered to be formed synchronously with mineralization, and on the zircon from the pre - existing alkali-altered granite. We discovered that the LA-ICP-MS U-Pb geochronology of the accessory minerals in the silicified fault zone and hydrothermal zircon in the granite reveals two Triassic hydrothermal activities at ∼235 Ma and ∼215 Ma, which are synchronous with regional Triassic magmatism. We therefore suggest the Triassic magmatism induced strong alkali metasomatism and the formation of silicified fault zones, which represents pre-ore, rather than syn-ore, hydrothermal activities. Mineral-element geochemistry shows that the ∼215 Ma granite has higher U concentrations than the ∼235 Ma granite. This implies that, in addition to fractional crystallization, repeated melting in the source is another important process that enhances magma fertility, as corroborated by thermodynamic modeling. The apatite from the silicified fault zone shows high Mn content (5,400–27,235 ppm), low δEu values (0.07–0.16), and high XF/XCl ratios (460–6,590). item.title: Time lag for arc volcanism following subduction initiation: A two-phase flow numerical modeling
item.dc:creator: Xinyi Zhong

item.description: Subduction initiation is a fundamental geodynamic process in plate tectonics, yet its mechanisms remain poorly understood due to the scarcity of geological records. Proposed geological records of subduction initiation, including metamorphic soles, fore-arc basalts and fore-arc sediments, are typically associated with spontaneous subduction initiation in hot environments involving mantle upwelling. In contrast, evidence for the more common cold subduction initiation at continental margins is sparse or even absent. Arc volcanic rocks are widely regarded as direct evidence of subduction zones, particularly for identifying ancient subduction zones in orogens. However, the temporal relationship between subduction initiation and the onset of arc volcanism remains poorly constrained. Although arc volcanism is generally considered to develop within ∼10 million years (Myr) of initiation, our analysis of subduction events over the past 15 Myr reveals a highly variable time lag ranging from 2 to 10 Myr. In this study, we investigate the factors controlling this time lag in forced subduction initiation at continental margins, using a newly developed two-phase flow numerical model that incorporates melt transport and melt extraction processes. Our results show that rapid partial melting at shallow depths, primarily driven by high convergence rates, leads to a shorter time lag between subduction initiation and arc volcanism, which is consistent with observations from recent subduction events. These findings suggest that arc volcanic rocks, when considered together with slab age and convergence rate, provide a useful constraint on the timing of subduction initiation in ancient subduction systems. item.description: The West Qinling gold metallogenic province is one of China’s largest gold producers, yet the genesis and temporal framework of its gold deposits remain highly debated. Variable bell-shape REE patterns and positive correlations between EuN and Eu* in scheelite indicate an oxidizing environment, controlled by variations in fluid salinity and Na-REE coupled substitution mechanism. Fluid inclusion microthermometry of coexisting scheelite and quartz shows consistent homogenization temperatures (163–307 ℃) and salinity (0.7–19.13 wt% NaCl equiv), implying a shared fluid origin. item.description: Earth’s continental crust is its most chemically evolved and diverse reservoir. Here, we report high-precision whole-rock Mo isotope data for 28 Archean granitoids from Australia’s Pilbara and Yilgarn cratons, with crystallization ages from 3.52 to 2.63 Ga. The samples cover a spectrum of magmatic series, including tonalite-trondhjemite-granodiorite (TTG), TTG hybrid, sanukitoid, potassic, and potassic hybrid magmas. After assessing the effects of alteration, crustal contamination, and fluid exsolution, we interpret the observed δ 98/95Mo range of − 0.93 to 0.25‰ as primarily reflecting magmatic source characteristics. TTG and TTG hybrid granitoids, together with samples derived from unenriched meta-mafic or mantle-like sources, have mean and median δ 98/95Mo values close to, or slightly higher than, chondrite and depleted MORB mantle (DMM). In contrast, potassic, potassic hybrid, and sanukitoid series granitoids, as well as samples derived from enriched meta-mafic or felsic crustal sources, extend to lower, sub-mantle δ 98/95Mo values. Elemental proxy relationships, major- and trace-element modeling, and phase-equilibrium constraints indicate that source composition and residual mineralogy during partial melting primarily control Mo isotope variability in these rocks. In crustally-derived granitoids, lower δ 98/95Mo values are associated with more mature source compositions and with changes in the abundance and composition of residual feldspar. Amphibole, garnet, and biotite may also have subordinate effects. These relationships suggest that Mo isotopes track the progressive reworking of Archean crust. Juvenile crust-derived TTG magmatism is characterized by near- to suprachondritic δ 98/95Mo, whereas later sanukitoid and potassic granitoid magmatism, linked respectively to mantle metasomatism and reworking of TTG-dominated gray gneiss, shifts toward lower δ 98/95Mo values. The observed trends imply that intracrustal reworking alone can push continental averages to sub-mantle values, with ramifications for mass-balance models. Although TTGs are generally suprachondritic, their δ 98/95Mo values are not high enough to easily support models requiring large volumes of Hadean to Paleoarchean continental extraction from a chondritic mantle to offset the subchondritic Mo isotope composition inferred for the depleted mantle from Archean komatiites. The strong Mo isotope contrast between continental crust and upper mantle may therefore have developed after 2.6 Ga, once crustal recycling became more extensive. item.description: The Söğüt gold deposit in northwestern Anatolia represents one of Türkiye's significant recent gold discoveries. Mineralisation is associated with pervasive Mg–Fe-rich alteration dominated by carbonate minerals, particularly dolomite, ankerite, and siderite. The results indicate that mineralisation formed at approximately 375 °C and 1.6 kbar from low-salinity, CO₂-bearing metamorphic fluids. We propose that episodic reactivation of the controlling shear zones caused transient pressure fluctuations and promoted fluid immiscibility, which together with wall-rock sulphidation and carbonatization, destabilised aqueous gold–bisulphide complexes and facilitated gold precipitation. item.description: The Socorro-Guaxupé Thrust Nappe (SGTN) is a metamorphic high-grade allochthonous terrane situated in southeast Brazil, interpreted as a segment of a Late Neoproterozoic magmatic arc that developed along the margin of a continental plate. The harzburgites record moderate degrees of partial melting (9–13%) and are composed of forsteritic olivine, enstatite, and minor spinel and diopside, later affected by serpentinization accompanied by magnetite and chlorite formation. The gabbros, locally containing hornblende, preserve primary igneous textures and consist mainly of calcic plagioclase (now completely saussuritized) and augite. These assemblages are overprinted by greenschist-facies metamorphism, characterized by actinolite, albite, epidote, and chlorite. Whole-rock major and trace element geochemistry of the metagabbros reveals two compositional groups, one slightly enriched and the other depleted in light rare earth elements (LREE), indicating affinities ranging from E-MORB to N-MORB.
